narrative.notes: Features: Appear human but lack eyes; perceive the world through the Force. Highly sensitive to Force disturbances, making them potentially crucial in an era where the Force's balance is shifting. True Blindness applies if in a Force-null area.

advantages.name: Danger Sense
advantages.description: You possess an instinctive ability to detect impending threats or danger. The GM will secretly roll against your Perception in situations involving ambushes, disasters, or similar hazards. On a success, you receive enough warning to take action. A roll of 3 or 4 provides additional detail about the danger. This early warning system primarily serves self-preservation, allowing you to react quickly whether to save allies or simply escape a trap. (Refer to GURPS Basic Set: Characters for full details.) Note: While a general advantage, for Force-sensitives, this often manifests as a subtle Force premonition. Prerequisite: Force Sensitive (if taken as a Force-related advantage, representing a Force-user's sensitivity to danger through the Force).

advantages.name: Field Detection (Miraluka)
advantages.description: Miraluka's intrinsic connection to the Force grants them an exceptional ability to perceive, analyze, and interact with energy fields. When a Miraluka character attempts a skill check to perceive, analyze, or interact with an energy field, their Field Detection ability grants them a significant mechanical advantage. Grant a +3 to +5 bonus to the Miraluka's relevant skill roll (e.g., Perception, Electronics Operation, Energy Weapon (Beam), or a specialized Force-related skill) when they are actively using Field Detection in an appropriate scenario. The specific bonus can be adjusted by the GM based on the complexity of the task or the Miraluka's Force sensitivity. This ability makes them expert saboteurs, security bypassers, or mechanics, capable of manipulating energy systems for various ends. Cost range: 5 points (Basic).

advantages.name: Force Sensitive (Racial Trait)
advantages.description: Some species are naturally attuned to the Force.

advantages.name: Force Sight (Miraluka Specialized Vision)
advantages.description: Miraluka do not perceive light, but instead "see" via their connection to the Force. This unique form of perception allows them to bypass many conventional visual obstructions such as darkness, smoke, and even some non-Force-resistant solid objects at close range (at the GM's discretion, based on the Miraluka's Force sensitivity). Effect for Miraluka: Miraluka characters possess an inherent and passive form of Force Sight as a racial trait. They always perceive the world through the Force and intrinsically possess 360-degree vision. For Miraluka, using their Force Sight does not cost Force Points (FP). Purchasing levels in the Force Sight Power (as detailed in Chapter 8: Force Powers) for a Miraluka primarily enhances the range and specific Force-related perceptive abilities of their natural Force Sight, rather than granting the basic ability to "see" through the Force. This unique vision allows for unparalleled situational awareness, making them superb scouts, spies, or tactical commanders, regardless of loyalty.

advantages.name: Ambidexterity
advantages.description: You are equally skilled with both hands (or equivalent appendages), suffering no off-hand penalty. Allows for versatile combat, dual-wielding, or multi-tasking under duress, enhancing efficiency regardless of the task's moral alignment.

advantages.name: Combat Reflexes
advantages.description: You react quickly to threats and keep your composure under pressure. Grants a +1 bonus to active defenses, +2 to Fright Checks, and a +6 bonus to the IQ roll to recover from mental stun (Chapter 9). Those two bonuses are the whole of what steadiness buys: it makes freezing less likely and shorter, and does not make you immune to either. Turn order is unaffected; it is set by Basic Speed and is never rolled for (Chapter 7). Prerequisite: Force Sensitive (if taken as a Force-related advantage, representing a Force-user's enhanced combat intuition).

disadvantages.name: Blind (Non-Conventional)
disadvantages.description: While Miraluka do not possess physical eyes and perceive the world through the Force, they are still considered "blind" in the conventional sense. This means they cannot see by means of light. They rely entirely on their Force Sight for perception. In areas where the Force is significantly diminished or nullified (e.g., a ysalimiri void), a Miraluka would be truly blind and severely impaired, relying on other senses or technological aids. This is typically a 0-point racial disadvantage because their Force Sight largely compensates for it, but the vulnerability remains.

disadvantages.name: Bloodlust
disadvantages.description: You have a compulsive urge to kill or inflict grievous harm in combat.

disadvantages.name: Charitable
disadvantages.description: You are acutely aware of others’ emotions, and feel compelled to help those around you - even legitimate enemies. Make a self-control roll in any situation where you could render aid or are specifically asked for help, but should resist the urge. If you fail, you must offer assistance, even if that means violating orders or walking into a potential trap.

disadvantages.name: Fanaticism
disadvantages.description: The character holds an unshakeable, unquestioning devotion to a cause, belief, or group. This can lead to extreme actions and a disregard for personal safety or the well-being of others outside their cause. This single-mindedness can be easily exploited by those who can frame their agenda as serving your cause.

disadvantages.name: Guilt Complex
disadvantages.description: You feel responsible for things that are not your fault, often leading you to take unnecessary blame or risks to atone for perceived failings.

disadvantages.name: Megalomania
disadvantages.description: You believe you are a superman, that you have been chosen for some great task, or that you are destined to conquer.  Even if you are a superhuman, this represents a single-minded pursuit of some fantastic goal, treating ordinary humans with contempt, or regarding yourself as a god.

disadvantages.name: Overconfidence (Martial)
disadvantages.description: The character can sometimes be overly confident in their martial prowess, believing their disciplined training and ability to read opponents makes them superior. This can lead them to underestimate foes, dismiss non-combat solutions, or take unnecessary risks in combat against unconventional threats.

disadvantages.name: Sense of Duty (A People)
disadvantages.description: You feel a strong obligation to members of a race.

disadvantages.name: Motion Sickness
disadvantages.description: You are miserable when in a moving vehicle. You may never learn any vehicle-operation skill. You must roll vs. HT as soon as you are aboard a moving vehicle. On a failure, you vomit and are at -5 on all DX, IQ, and skill rolls for the rest of the journey. On a success, you are merely miserably queasy and at -2 on DX, IQ, and skill rolls. Roll daily on long journeys.

disadvantages.name: Selfish
disadvantages.description: You prioritize your own needs and desires above those of others. This makes you unreliable in a team and potentially willing to betray others for personal gain, but also predictable to those who can appeal to your self-interest.

quirks.name: Broad-minded
quirks.description: You are exceptionally open to new ideas, cultures, and alien customs, rarely passing judgment.

forcePowers.description: The Miralukan species is a force sensitive humanoid race born without eyes, who perceive the world through the Force. This aids them in bypassing blindness, illusions, or even physical obstructions like smoke, darkness, or physical objects.
forcePowers.name: Miralukan Force Sight
forcePowers.effect: Range extends to 75 feet. You can detect living beings through thin objects within 5 yards. Gain +1 to Perception to detect hidden opponents.
forcePowers.requirements: Required Advantage: Force Sight (Miraluka Specialized Vision)

forcePowers.name: Farsight
forcePowers.description: The Force-user can extend their senses beyond normal limits, perceiving events and locations at great distances through the Force, as if physically present.
forcePowers.effect: Project senses to any location on the same planet for 5 minutes.

forcePowers.name: Psychometry
forcePowers.effect: By touching an object with a strong, recent history, you gain vague sensory hints of its past for 1 minute.
Gain +4 to Basic Move and +1.0 Basic Speed for 1d+1 turns. Gain +1 to Active Defenses.
forcePowers.description: The Force-user accelerates their body and mind, allowing them to move and react with incredible swiftness.
forcePowers.name: Force Speed

forcePowers.effect: By touch, inflict 1d-3 HP of injury that bypasses DR, and you heal for the exact amount lost.
forcePowers.name: Drain Life
Force Mind Trick
forcePowers.effect: Plant a simple, non-harmful suggestion in one non-Force-sensitive being within 5 feet. Requires a Quick Contest of skill vs. Will.

lightsaberForms.name: Form II: Makashi
lightsaberForms.effect: You gain a +2 bonus to Feint skill rolls and a +2 bonus to your Parry score against a single opponent. Your thrusting attacks with a lightsaber inflict +2 damage. On a successful Parry, your next attack against that opponent this turn gains a +1 skill bonus.

conditional.when: on thrusting attacks with a lightsaber
on your next attack against that opponent, after a successful Parry

lightsaberForms.name: Form III: Soresu
lightsaberForms.effect: You gain a +2 bonus to all Active Defenses. When parrying a blaster bolt, on a successful Lightsaber Combat skill roll, you may choose to redirect the bolt at a new target within 5 yards (requires a separate attack roll at -4 skill, or a simple straight deflection).
